10fw2ni:250: ChatGPT Search distinguishes between "real-time web information" and "pre-trained knowledge," providing citations only for the former. The engineering challenge behind this design choice is that the model must accurately determine which knowledge comes from training data (no citation) and which comes from the live web (should be cited). When the model confuses these two sources, users see "uncited statements that look factual" or "content that is cited but actually comes from training data." This boundary blurring is especially problematic in fast-moving fields (such as AI news and technology updates): the model's training data may be outdated, yet users cannot tell whether a "cited" piece of information is genuinely scraped from the live web, or whether the model has "disguised" old knowledge as newly cited information.
